vat.note: Approximate average standard VAT rate across EU member states. Applied once to the whole pump price.

fx.note: Approximate USD per EUR, October 2026. Replace with the ECB reference rate on each data refresh.

diesel.note: Simple average of 27 national averages, EU Weekly Oil Bulletin.

source.label: fuel-prices.eu, from the EC Weekly Oil Bulletin

petrol.note: Euro-super 95, simple average of 27 national averages, EU Weekly Oil Bulletin.

source.label: fuel-prices.eu, from the EC Weekly Oil Bulletin

vat.note: US fuel taxes are per gallon, so they drop out of the change.

diesel.note: No. 2 diesel, September 2026 monthly average, an all-time high.

brent.note: Approximate Brent price around 9 October 2026, read from a prediction market, not a settlement. Replace with an EIA or ICE settlement.

worldSupply.note: Approximate global oil supply. Replace with the latest IEA Oil Market Report figure.

priceFlexibility.note: Short-run % change in crude price per 1% change in supply, the inverse of a short-run demand elasticity of about 0.05 to 0.12. Assumption; the model is most sensitive to this.

exports.note: Seaborne crude 4.088 + seaborne products 1.075 mb/d, September 2026. Pipeline exports are excluded for lack of a sourced figure. They would also earn less at a lower world price, so leaving them out overstates the revenue gain somewhat.

discountNow.note: Urals discount to Brent assumed in the Russian Economy Ministry 2026 scenario.

discountRelief.note: Actual average Urals discount in 2025, used as the discount after sanctions relief.

maxExtraSupply.note: How much extra oil Russia could realistically put on the market. Production was about 10.4 mb/d in September 2026. Assumption.

stateTake.note: Share of export value that ends up in the Russian federal budget as extraction tax and other levies. Assumption; to be replaced with KSE Institute or CREA estimates.

oilGasRevenueMonth.note: Russian federal oil and gas budget revenue, September 2026 (RUB 452.4 bn). Used only as a sanity check.

unitCost.note: Production cost estimate for a Russian-built Geran-2 (Shahed-136).

source.label: Institute for Science and International Security, via DroneXL

longRangeLaunches.note: Drones launched at Ukraine in June 2026, Ukrainian Air Force data. Includes decoys, which lowers the per-launch ratio.

longRangeKilled.note: Civilians killed by long-range missiles and drones in June 2026.

longRangeInjured.note: Civilians injured by long-range missiles and drones in June 2026.

droneShare.note: Share of long-range casualties attributed to drones rather than missiles. HRMMU does not publish this split. Assumption.

childShareKilled.note: 7 of 293 civilians killed in June 2026 were children (all weapons).

source.label: UN HRMMU via Humanitarian Media Hub

childShareInjured.note: 116 of 1,990 civilians injured in June 2026 were children (all weapons).

source.label: UN HRMMU via Humanitarian Media Hub

latestMonth.label: August 2026
latestMonth.note: All civilian casualties verified by HRMMU in August 2026, all weapons.
